hero.headline: 11 workers killed in Washington paper mill chemical spill identified
hero.body:
A chemical tank rupture at a Nippon Dynawave Packaging facility in Longview, Washington killed 11 workers in an incident that shocked the local community. The implosion occurred early Tuesday morning at the mill, which sits along the Columbia River in the southwestern Washington city.

The tank contained white liquor, an alkaline chemical solution used in paper manufacturing. The tank was approximately 60 percent full at the time it ruptured, according to fire officials. White liquor is made up mostly of sodium sulfide, sodium hydroxide and disodium carbonate and is used to break down wood chips into pulp during the paper-making process.

The initial emergency response confirmed one fatality and multiple injuries, including chemical burns. Eight employees and one firefighter sustained injuries described as critical or life-threatening. Nine plant employees were unaccounted for following the initial reports. All missing workers were later recovered, bringing the total death toll to 11.

The Nippon Dynawave facility operates as both a pulp and paper mill and liquid packaging plant. The plant employs approximately 1,000 workers and manufactures materials for tissues, printing paper, cups, plates, cartons and other products. The facility has been operating since 1953 and serves as a major employer in Longview, a city of about 38,000 people with deep historical ties to the timber and paper industries.

Following the tank rupture, white liquor spilled into a drainage ditch. State ecology department officials evaluated the environmental impact of the spill. However, authorities said the incident posed no direct threat to the surrounding community, and there was no immediate public danger from the chemical release.

The recovery operation involved multiple agencies and emergency responders working to locate and identify the missing workers. Fire Chief Scott Goldstein noted the personal impact on responders. "The people who are responders here have friends and relatives that work on site," he said. "It is something that is impactful, and we have support networks to support the workers as well as the emergency responders."

U.S. Senator Patty Murray of Washington responded to the disaster in a written statement. "My heart is with everyone who lost a loved one today, as well as the injured workers," she said, calling the implosion an "absolute tragedy."

The investigation into the cause of the tank rupture remained ongoing as authorities worked to determine what led to the failure and what safety measures were in place at the time. The Nippon Dynawave facility did not immediately respond to inquiries about the incident. As recovery efforts continued, the scene remained closed to the public while crews worked to mitigate environmental concerns related to the spilled chemical.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by his envoys
cards.body:
President Trump has asked for several amendments to the nuclear agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts, according to administration officials briefed on the matter. The request came during a Situation Room meeting held on Friday.

Trump wants to finalize the deal soon but is seeking to strengthen several provisions he considers important, particularly regarding Iran's nuclear material, according to two U.S. officials. His request has prompted another round of negotiations between the parties that could extend several more days.

The tentative agreement reached this week would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz if approved. Under the framework being discussed, the strait would reopen with no tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension. Iran would be permitted to freely sell oil during this period, with negotiations on its nuclear program to follow within 30 to 60 days.

In exchange, the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports. The agreement would also include an official declaration ending the war and could release approximately 25 billion dollars in frozen Iranian assets.

However, significant disagreements remain. Iran's Fars news agency, which is close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, reported that the Strait of Hormuz would remain under Iranian control. The agency stated that "the management of the Strait, determining the route, time, method of passage, and issuing permits will continue to be the monopoly and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran." It characterized Trump's assertions about the deal being nearly final as "inconsistent with reality."

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated Trump on his peace efforts and said Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the United States and Iran soon. Pakistan's army chief has been a key figure in the negotiations and recently held meetings with Iranian officials.

The negotiations represent a major foreign policy initiative for the Trump administration. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical waterway for global oil shipments, and its closure has had significant economic implications.

Trump announced that he had conducted phone discussions with leaders of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain, and Pakistan, as well as Turkey's president. He also spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Trump said he met with American negotiators including special envoy Steve Witkoff and adviser Jared Kushner to discuss the latest proposals. He stated he would only sign a deal "where we get everything we want," warning that if an agreement was not reached, the United States would resume strikes against Iran.

The timeline for completing the amendments and reaching a final agreement remains uncertain as both sides continue their discussions.

cards.headline: Zelensky expects major Russian attacks within 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President cites intelligence from U.S. and European allies warning of imminent strikes.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is bracing for a major attack from Russia that he expects to occur within the next 48 hours. He cited intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies in warning of the imminent strikes.

Zelensky said he believes the attacks will happen either tonight or tomorrow night. The warning comes as tensions between Ukraine and Russia remain high, with Ukrainian officials monitoring Russian military movements and preparing defensive measures based on the intelligence assessments from Western partners.

cards.headline: China's Factory Activity Contracts Further in Warning Sign for Economy
cards.teaser: Manufacturing data showed continued weakening in Chinese industrial production.
cards.body:
Factory activity in China deteriorated further, according to new economic data. The worsening manufacturing indicators represent a warning signal for the broader Chinese economy.

The decline in factory activity adds to concerns about China's economic growth trajectory. Manufacturing has been a key driver of Chinese economic expansion, and sustained weakness in the sector could have wider implications for global supply chains and trade.

cards.headline: UN adds Israeli and Russian forces to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: Annual report includes allegations of rape against detained Palestinians for the first time.
cards.body:
The United Nations has placed Israeli and Russian security forces on its annual blacklist for the first time, documenting credible allegations of sexual violence during armed conflict. The report includes accusations of rape against detained Palestinians.

The blacklist identifies 77 government and non-government parties suspected of systematic rape and sexual violence in conflict zones. This expansion marks a significant step in the UN's efforts to document and identify perpetrators of conflict-related sexual abuse.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo kills over 245 as aid agencies warn of rapid spread
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 65 people confirmed by health officials, with 246 suspected cases reported in Ituri province. The situation has prompted urgent international concern as the virus threatens to spread beyond the currently affected region.

The outbreak has centered on mining towns in Ituri province, an area that borders Uganda and South Sudan. The constant movement of people through these mining communities presents a significant challenge to containing the disease. Uganda has already confirmed cases, including a 59-year-old man who died in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention expressed alarm about the potential for further spread. The organization's director general, Dr Jean Kaseya, stated: "Given the high population movement between affected areas and neighbouring countries, rapid regional coordination is essential."

A major concern for health officials is the strain of Ebola involved in this outbreak. Testing by the DRC's national research laboratory detected the Bundibugyo strain in 13 of 20 samples examined. Unlike the more common Zaire strain found in previous DRC outbreaks, there is no licensed vaccine available for Bundibugyo. This strain has only caused two previous documented outbreaks, in 2007 and 2012.

The World Health Organization estimates the death rate of this outbreak at between 30 and 50 percent among confirmed cases. Anaïs Legand from the WHO's high threat pathogens team noted: "It's huge. It means that up to five out of 10 people are likely to die."

Ituri province presents particularly difficult conditions for disease control. The region is a conflict zone experiencing ongoing fighting between armed groups, and medical facilities remain modest. Displaced people fleeing the violence are being forced into overcrowded camps, further complicating transmission prevention efforts.

Health workers lack adequate equipment to properly isolate patients and trace contacts. Aid agencies including Doctors Without Borders are mobilizing resources to support front-line health workers treating Ebola patients and investigating suspected cases. The organization described the virus's spread as deeply alarming.

The World Health Organization's director general visited the affected region to assess the situation and support response efforts. Officials convened an urgent meeting involving authorities from the DRC, Uganda, South Sudan, the WHO, and pharmaceutical companies to coordinate a regional response.

The DRC has experienced 16 documented Ebola outbreaks since the virus was identified there in 1976. Previous experience has shown that successful containment requires rapid case identification, patient isolation, and prevention of transmission to healthcare workers and family members. The international health community recognizes that coordinated responses involving multiple countries and organizations are essential to bringing this outbreak under control.

cards.headline: Drone crashes into Romanian apartment building as war spills across border
cards.teaser: A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war into civilian homes.
cards.body:
A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania early Friday morning, causing an explosion and fire. Residents have begun returning to check on their homes in the damaged block.

The incident has heightened fears among people living near the Ukrainian border. Residents expressed that no one feels safe now, as the Russia-Ukraine conflict continues to pose direct dangers to neighboring communities in Romania.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe ongoing killings in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers gave rare accounts to reporters describing continued combat operations in Gaza after a ceasefire was announced.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided accounts to the Associated Press describing continued military operations in Gaza following the ceasefire announcement. Multiple soldiers characterized the situation skeptically, with one stating that calling it a ceasefire is inaccurate given ongoing operations on the ground.

The soldiers' firsthand descriptions offer insight into the reality of deployment in Gaza, where combat activities have persisted despite the ceasefire agreement. An Israeli commander also told reporters that Hezbollah had developed plans for attacks on Israel similar to those carried out by Hamas.

cards.headline: Rescuers free five men trapped over a week in flooded Laos cave
cards.teaser: Four men were freed in a rescue operation from a flooded cave in Laos, with search efforts continuing for two still missing.
cards.body:
Divers have rescued five of seven men trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for 10 days. The miners had entered narrow tunnels on May 20 in search of gold when the cave flooded. One man was rescued on Friday, followed by four more in a subsequent operation described as perilous.

Two villagers remain missing as rescue teams continue navigating through muddy, narrow passages filled with sharp rocks. Rescuers have had to drain water from the cave system and manage collapse hazards to reach the trapped miners.

cards.headline: Japan defense minister rejects Chinese claims of militarism, cites Beijing's arms buildup
cards.teaser: Japan's defense minister pushed back against accusations of new militarism and pointed to China's own military expansion.
cards.body:
Japan's defense minister Koizumi rejected Chinese accusations of new militarism, countering that Beijing's own military expansion poses greater concern. The rebuke came during a security meeting following criticism from Chinese leader Xi Jinping, who had characterized Japan's defense policies as remilitarization during talks with Donald Trump.

Koizumi emphasized Japan's commitment to candid dialogue while highlighting China's rapid arms buildup as a strategic issue requiring attention.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested in France after Champions League celebrations turn violent
cards.teaser: French police arrested hundreds after crowds celebrating Paris Saint-Germain's victory over Arsenal fired flares and clashed with officers.
cards.body:
Hundreds of people were arrested in France as celebrations of Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal descended into unrest. Thousands of police officers were deployed to control crowds across multiple locations as fans celebrated in the streets.

The celebrations turned wild as some fans fired flares. Police worked to quell the disorder and manage the clashes that erupted between fans and law enforcement during the festivities.

cards.headline: Drone crashes into Romanian apartment building as war spills across border
cards.teaser: A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war into civilian homes.
cards.body:
A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania early Friday morning, causing an explosion and fire. Residents have begun returning to check on their homes in the damaged block.

The incident has heightened fears among people living near the Ukrainian border. Residents expressed that no one feels safe now, as the Russia-Ukraine conflict continues to pose direct dangers to neighboring communities in Romania.

cards.headline: Chinese-born woman's arrest in Taiwan sparks debate over security and profiling
cards.teaser: A woman from mainland China accused of infiltration has triggered discussion in Taiwan over balancing security with treatment of Chinese migrants.
cards.body:
Taiwan arrested a Chinese-born woman on accusations of infiltration, setting off a debate about how the island defends itself against potential threats from mainland China. The case has focused attention on spouses from China who have moved to Taiwan.

The arrest has raised questions about whether Taiwan can protect its democracy without profiling migrants who were born in China. Mainland spouses have become a focal point in discussions about infiltration fears as tensions between Taiwan and China continue.

cards.headline: Family of four killed in Virginia crash on way to wedding, bus driver charged
cards.teaser: A family of four traveling to a wedding died in a Virginia crash that killed five people total.
cards.body:
Five people died in a crash in Virginia that involved a family of four who were traveling to attend a wedding. The bus driver involved in the collision has been charged in connection with the incident.

The crash claimed the lives of the family members who were en route to a wedding celebration. A fifth person also died in the collision. Authorities have not released the identities of the victims or details about where the crash occurred in Virginia.

cards.headline: Protesters clash with police at New Jersey immigration detention facility
cards.teaser: Demonstrators outside an immigration detention center in Newark clashed with law enforcement after the governor called for calm.
cards.body:
Protests continued outside Delaney Hall, an immigration detention facility in Newark, New Jersey, as a hunger and labor strike inside reached its ninth day. Detained immigrants are demanding improved conditions and medical care. State police deployed barricades to separate groups demonstrating at the facility.

On Saturday morning, counterprotesters wearing Trump hats gathered in support of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, while other protesters advocated for the detained immigrants. The two groups faced off across police barricades, with state police present at the scene.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump plans for Kennedy Center renovation
cards.teaser: A federal judge issued a ruling that stopped the Trump administration's plans for changes at the Kennedy Center.
cards.body:
A judge blocked plans by the Trump administration to renovate the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The ruling angered Trump, who has publicly expressed frustration about the decision and the judge who issued it. Protests against the Trump-led changes at the Kennedy Center turned into a gathering outside the venue.

The legal setback for the administration involves proposed changes to the Washington cultural institution. Multiple outlets have analyzed the implications of the ruling, with The Atlantic describing the Kennedy Center as entering uncertain territory. Trump has vented about both the judge's decision and his broader legal challenges.

cards.headline: Trump seeks changes to Iran agreement negotiated by his envoys
cards.teaser: The president is requesting edits to an Iran deal that his own negotiating team worked out.
cards.body:
Trump is requesting modifications to an Iran peace framework that his own negotiating team developed. The changes reportedly focus on stricter terms for Iran, particularly around its uranium stockpile.

Trump met with his cabinet to make a final determination on the deal. According to observers, the self-proclaimed dealmaker has struggled to advance negotiations without undermining his own team's progress, even as Iran has strengthened its negotiating position.

cards.headline: Trump administration clarifies green card policy after confusion
cards.teaser: Federal officials appeared to walk back earlier messaging about requirements for immigrants seeking green cards.
cards.body:
The Department of Homeland Security said most immigrants will not need to leave the United States to obtain green cards, backing away from earlier statements that suggested otherwise. The initial policy announcement had prompted anxiety and confusion among immigrants and immigration attorneys.

The Trump administration's messaging about changes to green card procedures created uncertainty about who would be required to depart the country during the application process. CBS News reported that the administration appeared to downplay the impact of the policy changes after the initial rollout generated concern.

cards.headline: Four inmates escape from Alabama correctional facility
cards.teaser: Authorities are searching for four prisoners who got out of a detention center in Alabama.
cards.body: Four inmates escaped from a correctional center in Alabama, prompting a search by authorities. The prisoners fled the facility, and law enforcement agencies are working to locate and recapture them. The search is currently underway across the area surrounding the facility.

hero.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes at Florida Launch Site Hours After Winning National Security Contract
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Launch Complex 36 in Florida on Thursday evening. The explosion occurred at 9 p.m. ET and created a massive fireball that destroyed the launchpad. The blast was visible from over 100 miles away, with an orange sky reported in Fort Pierce and a glow seen as far north as South Carolina.

The timing proved particularly significant. Just hours before the explosion, Blue Origin had received a national security launch task order from NASA. The company had been positioned as a major competitor to SpaceX for government space contracts.

Jeff Bezos, Blue Origin's founder, confirmed on social media that all employees were safe and accounted for. "Very rough day, but we'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying," Bezos said. "It's worth it." The company described the incident as an "anomaly" but has not yet disclosed the root cause.

The explosion has direct consequences for NASA's lunar ambitions. The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle Blue Origin plans to use to launch lunar landers for NASA's Artemis program, including the landers that will carry astronauts to the moon's surface. NASA announced on Tuesday that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned missions this year to help construct NASA's 20 billion dollar moon base.

Jared Isaacman, NASA's administrator, stated that the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the program timeline following the incident. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," Isaacman wrote. He committed to working with partners to support an investigation and assess impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programs.

The explosion marks the latest in a series of setbacks for Blue Origin. Last month, a payload from the third New Glenn flight ended up in the wrong orbit, leading to a temporary FAA grounding. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight.

Shockwaves from the explosion were felt across Florida's space coast, with residents reporting shaking homes and taking to social media for information. Emergency officials reported no threat from fumes or other hazards. Flames continued burning at the launchpad more than two hours after the explosion.

The incident occurred as Blue Origin and SpaceX compete for NASA contracts under the Artemis program. Both companies have built facilities near Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions. Artemis III, scheduled for 2027, will test Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander against SpaceX's Starship system to determine which will transport astronauts to the lunar surface during the Artemis IV mission planned for 2028.

cards.headline: SoftBank Plans Up to $75 Billion Investment in AI Data Centers in France
cards.teaser: The Japanese conglomerate announced plans to build what would become Europe's largest artificial intelligence facility.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build AI data centers in France, what the company describes as Europe's largest AI facility. The investment represents a significant expansion of AI infrastructure across the continent.

The company aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity through this commitment. Founder Masayoshi Son outlined the company's strategy to strengthen its position in Europe's growing AI sector.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Attempts to Breach Cockpit
cards.teaser: A Chicago to Minneapolis flight was rerouted to Wisconsin following multiple attempts by a passenger to access the flight deck.
cards.body:
United Airlines flight 2005 was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin during a flight from Chicago to Minneapolis after a passenger made multiple attempts to breach the cockpit. The 75-year-old man's actions triggered a hijacking alert from the crew.

The aircraft landed safely in Madison, where the unruly passenger was detained by authorities. The diversion disrupted the planned route and travel for those aboard the flight.

cards.headline: China's Factory Activity Contracts Further in Warning Sign for Economy
cards.teaser: Manufacturing data showed continued weakening in Chinese industrial production.
cards.body:
Factory activity in China deteriorated further, according to new economic data. The worsening manufacturing indicators represent a warning signal for the broader Chinese economy.

The decline in factory activity adds to concerns about China's economic growth trajectory. Manufacturing has been a key driver of Chinese economic expansion, and sustained weakness in the sector could have wider implications for global supply chains and trade.

cards.headline: New Car Sales Drop as One Million Buyers Exit U.S. Market
cards.teaser: Auto sales fell for the eighth consecutive month as demand weakens and fewer Americans can afford new vehicles.
cards.body:
The U.S. new car market has lost approximately one million buyers, according to industry data. Auto sales have crashed for eight straight months as both electric vehicle demand and overall purchasing power decline.

New car sales have stagnated despite automakers maintaining profitability, according to a recent report. Rising prices have made new vehicles increasingly out of reach for many Americans, with analysts suggesting these buyers are unlikely to return to the market in the near term.

cards.headline: Ferrari Faces Criticism Over First Electric Vehicle Design
cards.teaser: The Italian automaker's inaugural EV, the Luce, has drawn negative reactions from critics and enthusiasts.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first electric vehicle, named the Luce, has been heavily criticized since its reveal. The brand developed the EV as a response to Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers entering the luxury market.

Some critics say Ferrari has abandoned its traditional roots with the new electric model. The backlash represents a challenge for the iconic sports car maker as it attempts to transition into electrification while maintaining its brand identity.

cards.headline: Startups Offer Free Cleaning in Exchange for Video Recordings to Train AI
cards.teaser: Technology companies are paying people to film themselves doing household chores as they gather data for artificial intelligence systems.
cards.body:
Several startups are offering free apartment cleaning services to residents willing to be filmed during the process. The companies plan to use this footage to develop AI systems capable of understanding and automating household tasks like dishwashing and decluttering.

Beyond free cleaning offers, other tech companies are paying workers to record themselves performing routine chores for machine learning applications. These video datasets help train AI models to recognize and potentially replicate domestic work activities.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, producing sonic booms heard across New England
hero.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a powerful blast that startled residents across New England. NASA confirmed the incident, which generated a sonic boom equivalent to 300 tons of TNT.

The fireball broke apart just after 2pm local time at an altitude of 40 miles, according to NASA's deputy news chief Jennifer Dooren. The meteor was traveling at approximately 75,000 miles per hour when it fragmented in the atmosphere.

The explosion produced loud booms that echoed across a wide region, with reports coming from multiple states and even extending into Canada. Hundreds of residents heard and felt the sonic boom, which prompted widespread confusion before authorities identified the source as a meteor explosion.

Sonic booms from meteors occur when space rocks travel through the atmosphere faster than the speed of sound. The sudden compression of air creates the characteristic explosive sound that can travel for considerable distances.

No damage or injuries have been reported from the event. Because the meteor broke apart at high altitude, any debris that reached the ground did so in unpopulated areas or was too small to cause harm.

The incident reflects how regularly small space rocks enter Earth's atmosphere. According to NASA, most space rocks smaller than a football field break apart during atmospheric entry and burn up completely. Explosions from meteor fragments are rare occurrences, though meteorite falls happen frequently around the world.

"There could be some small fragments, but a lot of it would have burned up in the atmosphere," explained Brian Mitchell, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, to the Associated Press.

Residents who witnessed the event took to social media to share their experiences and seek explanations for the startling sounds and bright light. Many described the sudden noise as alarming, comparing it to various familiar sounds as they tried to understand what had happened.

The meteor explosion added to weekend celestial activity, with additional astronomical events visible in the night sky. The incident served as a reminder of Earth's exposure to space debris and the regular but largely unnoticed encounters with meteoroids entering the planet's atmosphere.

NASA's analysis of satellite data confirmed the event's origin and characteristics, providing residents with scientific explanation for the startling experience that had puzzled many across the New England region.

cards.headline: Nvidia to unveil first Windows PCs powered by its processors next week
cards.teaser: The first Windows computers running on Nvidia chips will debut next week, according to reports.
cards.body:
Nvidia will introduce the first Windows PCs powered by its own processors next week, according to Axios. The new systems will mark Nvidia's entry into the PC processor market, where it has previously focused on graphics cards.

Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm have posted cryptic messages on social media ahead of Nvidia's GTC event, teasing the new N1X laptop processors. The chips represent a collaboration between the three companies to develop Arm-powered Windows PC processors.

cards.headline: SoftBank announces plans to invest up to 75 billion in French data centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese conglomerate said it aims to develop up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank plans to invest up to €75 billion to build data centers across France, marking a significant expansion of the company's European infrastructure. The investment will support the development and operation of up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in the country.

This commitment demonstrates SoftBank's strategy to strengthen its computing infrastructure presence in Europe through large-scale data center operations.

cards.headline: Blue micromoon visible tonight as May's second full moon rises
cards.teaser: A rare blue micromoon will be visible this weekend, marking the second full moon of May.
cards.body:
A blue micromoon will rise tonight, marking the second full moon of May. The blue moon designation refers to the occurrence of two full moons within a single calendar month, rather than any actual change in the moon's color. Meanwhile, the micromoon label indicates the moon is at a more distant point in its orbital path around Earth.

Viewing conditions are expected to be favorable, with clear skies and a bright moon visible tonight. Multiple news organizations have provided guidance on the best times and methods for observing this rare celestial event.

cards.headline: AC unveils new Cobra Coupe with up to 799 horsepower
cards.teaser: The British automaker has released a production model of its Cobra Coupe with a supercharged V8 engine.
cards.body:
AC has officially debuted its new Cobra Coupe production model, returning the British icon with up to 720 horsepower according to some reports and 799 horsepower according to others. The two-seater sports car features a Ford 5.0-liter V8 engine.

The AC Cobra GT Coupe is priced at $315,000 according to Car and Driver, while The Supercar Blog reported a $500,000 price tag. The supercharged supercar represents AC's modern interpretation of the classic Cobra design with an enclosed roof configuration.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games on Switch 2
cards.teaser: The company issued a new wave of updates to improve how original Switch titles run on its newest console.
cards.body:
Nintendo has released a new wave of backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games running on the Switch 2. The updates address issues with games from the original Switch console playing on the newer hardware.

The fixes represent Nintendo's ongoing effort to ensure games from its previous generation console work properly on the Switch 2. The company has been rolling out compatibility improvements in waves since the new system's launch.

cards.headline: Scientists discover killer fungus that may restore habitats damaged by invasive moss
cards.teaser: A newly discovered fungus species could help reverse damage to native British ecosystems caused by invasive moss.
cards.body:
A newly discovered fungus species has raised hope that some native British habitats could be restored after damage from invasive moss. Scientists identified the fungus as a potential biological control agent.

The fungus targets invasive moss species that have decimated certain habitats. Researchers believe the discovery could provide a natural solution to restoring ecosystems without chemical interventions.

hero.headline: Spurs defeat Thunder in Game 7 to reach NBA Finals
hero.body:
The San Antonio Spurs advanced to the NBA Finals after defeating the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night. The victory sends the Spurs to face the New York Knicks, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs' charge against the defending champions. The 7-foot-4 Frenchman finished with 22 points and seven rebounds, earning him the Western Conference Finals MVP award. He became emotional after the final buzzer, reflecting on the significance of reaching the Finals. "Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," he said when asked about his tears. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

However, Wembanyama's teammates played crucial roles in the victory. Julian Champagnie scored 20 points and connected on six three-pointers. Dylan Harper made an impact off the bench, while Luke Kornet made a crucial defensive block in the fourth quarter as Oklahoma City mounted a comeback attempt. After the game, Wembanyama praised his supporting cast, saying "They don't know how much I love them, and everyone stepped up tonight."

The Thunder fought hard despite missing Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, was brilliant for Oklahoma City with 35 points and nine assists. Still, no other Thunder player scored more than 20 points as the defending champions saw their title hopes end.

Thunder coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the loss while maintaining confidence in his team. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he said. "And it's the NBA, there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

For the Spurs, the Finals matchup with New York carries historical significance. The teams last met in the 1999 NBA Finals, when San Antonio won the series 4-1. They also faced each other in the NBA Cup final earlier this season.

The Spurs secured the victory by controlling the final moments of the game. As the clock wound down and the Thunder were forced to launch desperate three-pointers from well beyond the arc, San Antonio sealed the win with a breakaway dunk.

Julian Champagnie captured the magnitude of the achievement after the final buzzer. "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen," he said.

San Antonio's last NBA championship came in 2014, while the Knicks have not won a title since 1973.

cards.headline: Claude Lemieux dies at 60, brain donated for CTE research
cards.teaser: The family of former NHL player Claude Lemieux announced his brain will be donated to Boston University's CTE Center.
cards.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion, died at age 60. His family announced that his brain will be donated to Boston University's CTE Center for chronic traumatic encephalopathy research.

Lemieux won four Stanley Cup championships during his NHL career. The donation will contribute to ongoing research into brain injuries and their long-term effects on athletes.

cards.headline: Finland defeats Canada to reach world championship final against Switzerland
cards.teaser: Finland advanced to the world championship final after beating Canada in the semifinals.
cards.body:
Finland will face Switzerland in the world championship final after defeating Canada in semifinal play. Panthers captain Aleksander Barkov led Finland to victory, advancing the team to the championship match.

Switzerland also won their semifinal matchup to set up the gold medal game against Finland.

cards.headline: Gable Steveson wins RAF wrestling debut by technical fall
cards.teaser: Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson defeated Alexander Romanov by technical fall in his RAF Wrestling debut.
cards.body:
Gable Steveson made a successful RAF Wrestling debut, securing a technical fall victory over Alexander Romanov at RAF 9. Merab Dvalishvili also delivered a dominant performance on the same card.

The event featured several notable matchups, including a bout between Colby Covington and Chris Weidman. Following the results, RAF announced that Arman Tsarukyan will face Colby Covington in July.

cards.headline: Darren Till knocks out Aaron Chalmers in BKFC debut
cards.teaser: Former UFC fighter Darren Till won his Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship debut with a one-punch knockout.
cards.body:
Darren Till defeated Aaron Chalmers by knockout in his first Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship appearance at BKFC 90. Till recovered from an early knockdown to land a decisive punch that ended the fight.

Rico Franco also won on the card, knocking out Connor Tierney to claim an interim title. Till's successful debut marks his transition from mixed martial arts to bare knuckle boxing.

cards.headline: Trump defends Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart after rally appearance
cards.teaser: President Trump responded to criticism of New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart's appearance at a political rally.
cards.body:
President Trump called critics of Jaxson Dart jealous after the New York Giants quarterback introduced him at a rally. The appearance sparked disagreement between Dart and teammate Abdul Carter, though both players later expressed unity.

Former NFL player Dez Bryant defended Dart's decision to appear at the rally, saying he does not understand the criticism directed at the quarterback. Dart introduced the president at the political event.

cards.headline: Arsenal prepares for title parade after Champions League final loss
cards.teaser: Arsenal will celebrate their Premier League title with an open bus parade less than 24 hours after losing the Champions League final.
cards.body:
Arsenal will hold an open bus parade on Sunday to celebrate winning the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years, just hours after losing the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties.

Kai Havertz's early goal and a strong defensive display gave Arsenal hope of securing a double, but PSG equalized through Ousmane Dembélé in the second half. Arsenal missed two penalties in the shootout—including one from Gabriel Magalhães—as PSG claimed their second consecutive Champions League title. Manager Mikel Arteta said the team must use the pain from the loss and "turn it into fuel" for future success.

hero.headline: Search Suspended for Man Believed to Be 'Alaskan Bush People' Star Matt Brown
hero.body:
Authorities have suspended the search for a man believed to be Matt Brown, a star of the Discovery Channel reality series 'Alaskan Bush People,' following reports that he took his own life. Brown's brother Bear stated that Matt was spotted near a river where police say a man went missing.

Brown, who appeared on the reality show about a family living off the grid in Alaska, had reportedly been in the area before disappearing. The search operation was called off after investigators received information suggesting Brown may have died by suicide.

Local law enforcement had been conducting search efforts in the river area where witnesses reported seeing someone matching Brown's description. The suspension of the search indicates authorities believe they have gathered sufficient information about the circumstances surrounding the disappearance.

Brown was one of the original cast members of 'Alaskan Bush People,' which documented his family's attempts to live independently in remote wilderness areas. The show, which premiered in 2014, followed the Brown family through various challenges of off-grid living.

The Discovery Channel has not released a statement regarding the reports. Brown's family members, including his brother Bear, have been in contact with authorities during the investigation.

Brown had stepped away from the show in recent years. His brother's public statements about seeing him near the river have been part of the information authorities used in their investigation.

The case remains under investigation by local law enforcement, though active search operations have ended. Authorities have not released additional details about the evidence that led them to suspend the search or confirmed the identity of the missing person.

Family members and former cast members have not made extensive public comments beyond Bear Brown's initial statements about his brother's whereabouts near the river.

cards.headline: Trump Proposes Canceling Great American State Fair Concerts After Artists Drop Out
cards.teaser: Former President Trump suggested canceling music performances at the Great American State Fair after several artists withdrew from the event.
cards.body:
President Trump announced plans to replace a concert series with an "America Is Back" rally after multiple performers withdrew from the event. Artists including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels and country singer Martina McBride dropped out, citing concerns that the event would become political.

Trump made the announcement during a Saturday posting spree on Truth Social, in which he shared 25 posts within two hours. The rally is scheduled to take place next month at the Great American State Fair.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remainder of Four Seasons Farewell Tour
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old music legend canceled his remaining 2026 tour dates to focus on his health.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli has canceled all remaining dates of the Four Seasons' farewell tour through the end of 2026 due to health concerns. The 92-year-old music legend apologized to fans for the disappointment caused by the cancellation.

Valli said he needs to prioritize his health at this time. The farewell tour was meant to celebrate the legendary performer and his iconic group.

cards.headline: Horror Films from YouTube Directors Top Box Office
cards.teaser: The two biggest movies at the box office were both directed by filmmakers who started on YouTube.
cards.body:
The horror films 'Backrooms' and 'Obsession' dominated the weekend box office, both directed by creators who began their careers on YouTube. Jason Blum and James Wan discussed how the success of these low-budget horror films is saving the industry.

'Obsession' dethroned 'The Mandalorian And Grogu' at the box office. Blum compared the current low-budget horror boom to edgy movies from the 1970s, noting there is almost a feeling of that era returning. The films have become word-of-mouth sensations, with the Blumhouse-Atomic Monster partnership positioning itself as a potential Disney of horror.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Flips Piano During Denver Performance
cards.teaser: The country star overturned a piano onstage while performing 'Sand in My Boots' in Denver.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen flipped over a piano during a performance of 'Sand in My Boots' at a concert in Denver. The country music star appeared upset with the instrument during the show.

The incident occurred onstage in front of the audience. Wallen's actions drew comparisons to Billy Joel, though the specific circumstances that led to the piano flip were not detailed beyond his apparent frustration with the instrument.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Reflects on Liam Payne's Death
cards.teaser: The former One Direction member discussed his late bandmate in a new interview, sharing memories that make him laugh and feel sadness.
cards.body:
Niall Horan spoke about the death of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at age 31 after falling three floors from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Horan said there is sadness when he thinks about Payne, but it also makes him laugh and smirk because of the memories they shared. Horan revealed he was with Payne in Argentina just before his death. The singer reflected on their time together as members of One Direction.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Second Contestant in Two Years for Using Racial Slur
cards.teaser: Vasana Montgomery was dismissed from the reality dating show after social media posts surfaced showing her using the n-word.
cards.body:
Love Island USA removed cast member Vasana Montgomery from the upcoming season after social media posts surfaced of her using the n-word. Montgomery will not appear when the reality dating series returns to Peacock on June 2.

This marks the second consecutive year the show has dismissed an islander for the same reason. The removal occurred just two days before the season premiere. Producers acted after the offensive social media content was discovered.

hero.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by his envoys
hero.body:
President Trump has asked for several amendments to the nuclear agreement his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts, according to administration officials briefed on the matter. The request came during a Situation Room meeting held on Friday.

Trump wants to finalize the deal soon but is seeking to strengthen several provisions he considers important, particularly regarding Iran's nuclear material, according to two U.S. officials. His request has prompted another round of negotiations between the parties that could extend several more days.

The tentative agreement reached this week would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz if approved. Under the framework being discussed, the strait would reopen with no tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension. Iran would be permitted to freely sell oil during this period, with negotiations on its nuclear program to follow within 30 to 60 days.

In exchange, the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports. The agreement would also include an official declaration ending the war and could release approximately 25 billion dollars in frozen Iranian assets.

However, significant disagreements remain. Iran's Fars news agency, which is close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, reported that the Strait of Hormuz would remain under Iranian control. The agency stated that "the management of the Strait, determining the route, time, method of passage, and issuing permits will continue to be the monopoly and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran." It characterized Trump's assertions about the deal being nearly final as "inconsistent with reality."

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated Trump on his peace efforts and said Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the United States and Iran soon. Pakistan's army chief has been a key figure in the negotiations and recently held meetings with Iranian officials.

The negotiations represent a major foreign policy initiative for the Trump administration. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical waterway for global oil shipments, and its closure has had significant economic implications.

Trump announced that he had conducted phone discussions with leaders of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain, and Pakistan, as well as Turkey's president. He also spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Trump said he met with American negotiators including special envoy Steve Witkoff and adviser Jared Kushner to discuss the latest proposals. He stated he would only sign a deal "where we get everything we want," warning that if an agreement was not reached, the United States would resume strikes against Iran.

The timeline for completing the amendments and reaching a final agreement remains uncertain as both sides continue their discussions.

cards.headline: Zelensky expects major Russian attacks within 48 hours
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President cites intelligence from U.S. and European allies warning of imminent strikes.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is bracing for a major attack from Russia that he expects to occur within the next 48 hours. He cited intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies in warning of the imminent strikes.

Zelensky said he believes the attacks will happen either tonight or tomorrow night. The warning comes as tensions between Ukraine and Russia remain high, with Ukrainian officials monitoring Russian military movements and preparing defensive measures based on the intelligence assessments from Western partners.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks judge's recusal in Georgia election case
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors cite judge's attendance at event honoring Fani Willis as raising impartiality concerns.
cards.body:
The Justice Department asked a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing its lawsuit against Georgia election officials on Friday. Prosecutors argued that her attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial.

The request was submitted to the U.S. District Court. The Justice Department's motion centers on concerns that the judge's participation in the Willis event could create the appearance of bias in the case involving Georgia election officials.

cards.headline: UN adds Israeli and Russian forces to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: Annual report includes allegations of rape against detained Palestinians for the first time.
cards.body:
The United Nations has placed Israeli and Russian security forces on its annual blacklist for the first time, documenting credible allegations of sexual violence during armed conflict. The report includes accusations of rape against detained Palestinians.

The blacklist identifies 77 government and non-government parties suspected of systematic rape and sexual violence in conflict zones. This expansion marks a significant step in the UN's efforts to document and identify perpetrators of conflict-related sexual abuse.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor steps away from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutor who secured indictment against former FBI director withdraws from case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down from the case. A notice of substitution was filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina on Friday stating that Matthew, the lead prosecutor, is no longer handling the matter.

Comey faces charges for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a social media post of seashells that has since been deleted. The prosecutor's departure comes after obtaining the indictment, with a new attorney expected to take over the case.

cards.headline: Immigrant detainees sue over conditions at Texas ICE facility
cards.teaser: Lawsuit accuses federal government of inhumane treatment at Camp East Montana in El Paso.
cards.body:
A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Immigration and Customs Enforcement over conditions at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas, the largest immigration detention facility in the United States. Four detainees are serving as plaintiffs on behalf of all current and future civil detainees at the facility.

The complaint alleges severe violations of human and constitutional rights, citing inadequate medical and mental health care, misuse of force, excessive solitary confinement, poor food quality, disease outbreaks, unsanitary living conditions, and sexual harassment by guards. Legal organizations filed the lawsuit early Saturday, characterizing the facility's conditions as "dire" and "abhorrent."

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: Fund announced earlier this month has sparked backlash and exposed Republican Party fractures.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. The case was revived after a third-party motion challenged a settlement that established the $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund, claiming the deal represents collusion and fraud on the court.

The lawsuit was originally brought by Trump and his sons after their personal and business tax returns were leaked by a former IRS contractor. The reopened case will examine the settlement's legal validity and the fund's creation.
